 Galveston County District Court
 Cause No. 2026-CV-0037
 Christina Ellis, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Defendant's Original Answer
Date:
6-1-26
Counsel for defendant:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defendant responds to the allegations in Plaintiff's Original Petition as follows. Pursuant to Texas Rule of Civil
Procedure 92, Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and
demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence.
For further answer, and without assuming any burden of proof that the law places on Plaintiff, Defendant asserts the
following affirmative defenses.
First, the incident was caused in whole or in part by the negligence of Plaintiff, including failure to keep a proper
lookout, faliure to yield the right of way, and failure to maintain a safe distance from adjacent vehicles while Plaintiff
was operating a motor vehicle. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must
be reduced in proportion to Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility.
Second, Defendant invokes the proportionate responsibility provisions of Chapter 33, and requests that the tirer of
fact assign responsibility aomng all responsible parties, including any settling person or responsible third party
designated under Section 33.004.
Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by not following reasonable medical advice, by delaying treatment, or by
failing to pursue available care, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
